ports.note: Takes a table and gives back the same table with fewer rows. Key columns, value field and unit are unchanged, because selecting rows does not change what the table measures.

ontology.note: No ontology mapping yet. The receipt names the column, the values kept, how many rows were kept and dropped, and any named value the table did not hold.

changes.description: Keeps only the rows whose chosen key column holds one of the values named, in the order named. Nothing in the application selected rows of a table before: `clip_points_to_area` filters points by geometry and has no equivalent for a table. A value the table does not hold is reported rather than ignored, because asking for a row that is not there is usually a typo or a changed table upstream, and quietly returning fewer rows is how a figure loses a category nobody noticed. Keeping nothing the table holds is refused rather than returning an empty table.

evidence.note: Unit tested on the same Table IX fixture, including the ordering the named values impose and a value absent from the table. Nothing here establishes that a selection is an honest one: keeping a subset of categories is exactly how a figure can mislead, and the widget cannot tell a partition from a cherry-pick.
